Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34786

Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/1640

Candidate: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/pull/1547 at exact commit `ccabba009ecd391d7f97d50a7c1ca52b7490ac95`

Independent review: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/pull/1606

## What I found

I reproduced the review claims against the exact candidate before changing the prepared branch. Its three GPU tests pass and correctly validate helper-level selection for a fresh unset index, a mixed batch, and an explicit lazy speculative plan. They do not exercise allocation or a speculative boundary crossing.

The prepared `main` source already contains both the `None -> 0` guard and the complete lazy speculative lifecycle. No additional runtime source change was justified. This correction preserves the candidate tests and adds a lifecycle regression using the real production methods for fresh-request ping-pong allocation, lazy speculative pending-slot allocation, TARGET_VERIFY metadata construction, and confirmed-boundary promotion/freeing. It checks exact GPU-resident slot values and state transitions.

## Failing before / passing after

The historical tensor expression still reproduces the original failure deterministically:

```text
TypeError: 'NoneType' object cannot be interpreted as an integer
```

Commands:

```bash
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-96f5d9ca8c97/venv/bin/python reports/j-96f5d9ca8c97/reproduce_pre_fix.py
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-96f5d9ca8c97/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_mamba_track_indices.py
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-96f5d9ca8c97/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_schedule_batch_prepare_for_decode.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_batch_result_processor_mamba_boundary.py
```

Results: the pre-fix expression reproduced the TypeError; the consolidated regression passed 4 tests; adjacent lifecycle coverage passed 3 tests and 2 subtests. GPU execution used one AMD Instinct MI350X (`gfx950`).

## Limitations

No fresh-request hybrid-mamba model was served end to end. Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 weights, the reported two RTX 3090 GPUs, NVIDIA behavior, and multi-GPU behavior were unavailable. The existing Qwen3-Next MTP lazy serving test requires a four-GPU model environment and was not run. The tiny Llama fixture is not hybrid-mamba and was not used as proof. The added test validates scheduler/cache allocation and boundary lifecycle, not model semantics, HTTP serving, or distributed execution. No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.

Complete evidence and the structured result are under `reports/j-96f5d9ca8c97/`.
